He pledged to accommodate the island's realities but took a hard line against separatism.

articles.title: Kimberly Powell: Nvidia career in spotlight
articles.summary: Kimberly Powell has spent 18 years at Nvidia, moving from medical imaging to some of the company's biggest healthcare AI projects, including genomics and drug discovery. But the 48-year-old vice president is now in the headlines for a different reason.The New York Times reported on November 11 that she had an intimate relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, 63, who is her direct boss. The report cited five people who worked at the company and said the two were seen being affectionate in a video recorded at a San Jose hotel during an Nvidia conference in March. Powell is married, the newspaper reported.When the Times asked Huang about his relationship with Powell, he reportedly replied, "I don't think you should be talking to me directly," before ending the call. Powell and Nvidia had not responded to Business Insider's requests for comment as of November 12. Neither has confirmed the reported relationship.The report comes as Nvidia is already dealing with another controversy involving Huang. The CEO recently told employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without naming anyone.Separately, the company's board has been examining whether a technology executive with alleged links to Chinese intelligence targeted Huang. That case involves Alice Huang, not Kimberly Powell. Together, the developments have put the company's leadership, internal policies and board oversight under fresh scrutiny.Who is Kimberly Powell and what is her role at Nvidia?Powell is one of Nvidia's senior executives responsible for taking its AI computing technology beyond conventional chip applications. Her current role covers healthcare and life sciences, two areas where Nvidia wants to expand the use of accelerated computing and artificial intelligence.        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Yahoo Finance (@yahoofinance)She joined Nvidia in 2008 as a director. Her initial responsibility was to establish Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) as computing accelerators for medical imaging equipment.Before joining Nvidia, Powell worked in hardware engineering and product management at Planar Systems, where she focused on diagnostic imaging systems. She holds a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, with a concentration in computer engineering, from Northeastern University.Her entry into Nvidia was not the result of a conventional executive recruitment process. On an August 2026 episode of the Lifers podcast, she explained that she had contacted Nvidia to discuss its computing technology. The company subsequently recognised its potential applications in healthcare and approached her about joining.She described the opportunity as a "dream come true."Powell's responsibilities grew over the years. Her LinkedIn profile says she became a senior director in 2016, leading an AI-focused business development team. In 2017, she was promoted to vice president of healthcare.When she joined in 2008, one of the main opportunities was using GPUs to process medical images. Medical imaging systems generate large volumes of data, and GPUs can process many calculations simultaneously. This makes them useful for applications such as analysing CT scans, MRI images and other diagnostic images.Over time, Nvidia expanded this approach into other parts of healthcare.Its medical imaging platform, MONAI, provides tools for developing AI applications that analyse medical images. Its BioNeMo platform supports AI research in biology and drug discovery. Parabricks uses accelerated computing to process genomic data.Powell's role has therefore expanded from promoting GPUs for imaging equipment to developing a wider computing and software ecosystem for healthcare companies, hospitals and pharmaceutical researchers.According to her profile on the Milken Institute's website, she also oversees the global strategy and commercial expansion of these platforms.Kimberly Powell report and Alice Huang investigationThe Powell report is the second major development involving Huang's personal relationships to emerge during Nvidia's current leadership crisis. But the two cases concern different women and different allegations.The first involves Alice Huang, a technology executive associated with Megaspeed. The New York Times previously reported that US officials believed she might have been recruited by the Chinese government to gather information about Nvidia.The allegations have raised national security questions because Nvidia makes some of the world's most advanced AI chips, which are subject to US export restrictions on sales to China.Nvidia's board launched an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The company has also faced scrutiny over its relationship with Alice Huang and the circumstances surrounding the alleged intelligence operation.The issue has also reached Congress. Republican lawmakers have sought a closed-door briefing from Huang on his relationship with Alice Huang and the national security concerns surrounding Nvidia's business in China.On November 11, Reuters reported that Nvidia's board had met to consider whether Huang should be removed as CEO. The Wall Street Journal separately reported that the board was preparing to oust him.Nvidia has 11 board members, including Huang. Under the company's bylaws, a majority of directors can remove him, with or without cause. All directors other than Huang are considered independent.As of November 12, no final removal decision had been publicly announced.Reuters also reported that there was no obvious successor if Huang were removed. Nvidia's CFO Colette Kress and senior data-centre executive Ian Buck have been mentioned in discussions about possible leadership arrangements, but no successor has been announced.Nvidia is scheduled to report its quarterly results on November 17.Nvidia shares closed at $173.73 on November 11, gaining 2.87% during the regular session. However, the stock fell more than 8% in extended trading after reports that the board was considering Huang's future.Reuters reported that Nvidia shares also fell around 7% in early Frankfurt trading on November 12. The company's market value had declined by roughly $600 billion since the board announced its investigation into the Alice Huang matter, according to the report.

Andhra urges Walmart to source from MSMEs
articles.summary: On Thursday, Andhra Pradesh called on American retail major Walmart to expand its local procurement by bringing the state's MSMEs, women-led self-help groups (SHGs), and artisans into its supply network.The request was made during discussions between Andhra Pradesh's IT and HRD Minister Nara Lokesh and Paul Dyck, Walmart's Senior Vice President for Global Government Affairs and Business Diplomacy, who met on the sidelines of the 31st CII Partnership Summit."Andhra Pradesh is asking Walmart and Flipkart to widen their sourcing from the State beyond seafood and pharmaceuticals, to include its MSMEs, women-led self-help groups and artisans," an official statement noted.To build on the momentum of the New Delhi Walmart Growth Summit—which linked Indian vendors with the retailer's international buying teams, Lokesh proposed that Walmart host a specialized MSME sourcing event in Andhra Pradesh centered on seafood and textiles. He further recommended establishing a dedicated pipeline within Walmart and Flipkart’s domestic and international supply chains for goods produced by local artisans and women-led SHGs, specifically those marketed under the state's Swayam AP and Lepakshi labels.According to the official release, Dyck acknowledged that Walmart ranks among the top purchasers of Andhra Pradesh shrimp, buying over 65 million pounds annually, while also procuring textiles, engineering goods, and pharmaceuticals from the region.Furthermore, Flipkart's regional footprint has generated over 28,000 direct and indirect employment opportunities. Its operational infrastructure includes over 100 logistics hubs covering roughly 12 lakh sq ft, alongside 0.33 million sq ft dedicated to wholesale operations. Through a memorandum of understanding with the AP MSME Corporation and the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub (RTIH), over 3,200 MSMEs have received training, resulting in more than 900 businesses actively selling on the Walmart and Flipkart platforms.Dyck assured that Walmart would review the state's recommendations."Walmart is already one of the largest buyers of Andhra Pradesh shrimp. Now we want them to look at the rest of what our State makes. Our MSMEs, women's groups and artisans make products of global quality. What they need is a direct line to global buyers, and Walmart and Flipkart can provide it," said Lokesh.

articles.title: India’s Russian fossil fuel imports hit record
articles.summary: India was the second-largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels in October, purchasing hydrocarbons worth €6.4 billion, according to a monthly analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA). It was India’s highest monthly total in data going back to January 2022.Crude oil accounted for 91% of India’s purchases at €5.8 billion. Coal imports were worth €333 million, while oil products accounted for €232 million.Indian refineries raise Russian crude purchasesIndia’s imports of Russian crude oil rose 10% from September. Imports increased at all three of the country’s largest importing refineries—Vadinar, Jamnagar and Paradip.Imports at Vadinar rose 12% month-on-month, while Jamnagar and Paradip recorded increases of 22% and 28%, respectively. The rise made Jamnagar the biggest importer of seaborne Russian crude in October.Refineries in India, Turkiye and Brunei that use Russian crude exported oil products worth €1.6 billion to countries imposing sanctions in October. The destinations included the European Union, Australia, the US and New Zealand.Ten of the 12 shipments of oil products from refineries processing Russian crude that reached EU ports in October departed from India’s Jamnagar refinery. The remaining two shipments came from Turkiye’s STAR refinery.CREA estimated that €389 million worth of the oil products exported by these refineries were made from Russian crude. Exports from the refineries to sanctioning countries rose 21% in volume terms from September.Russia’s fossil fuel earnings reach four-year highChina remained the largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels, purchasing €10.7 billion worth of hydrocarbons in October. The European Union was the third-largest buyer at €2.2 billion, followed by Turkiye at €1.1 billion and South Korea at €488 million.Russia’s total fossil fuel export revenues rose 14% month-on-month to €754 million per day in October, the highest monthly level since December 2022. Export volumes remained broadly unchanged.Crude oil export revenues rose 19% to €449 million per day, with seaborne crude earnings increasing 23% to €352 million per day. CREA said this was the highest monthly level recorded since its data series began in January 2022.The report said higher global oil prices, linked to the energy crisis around the Strait of Hormuz, helped increase Russia’s fossil fuel earnings. Russia’s Urals crude averaged $101.70 a barrel in October, more than twice the EU and UK price cap of $44.10 a barrel.CREA also said that 60% of Russia’s seaborne oil was transported by sanctioned “shadow” tankers in October. Another 37% was carried by tankers owned or insured in G7 countries and their partners.A crude oil price cap of $30 a barrel, if fully enforced, would have reduced Russia’s seaborne crude oil export revenues by 21%, or €2.2 billion, in October, CREA said. A lower cap on crude and oil products together could have reduced Russia’s total seaborne oil export revenues by 25%, or €3.4 billion.

articles.title: Ola Electric shares jump 7% ahead of Q2 results, extends EV-policy rally
articles.summary: Shares of Ola Electric Mobility jumped more than 7% on Thursday ahead of the EV scooter-maker’s Q2 earnings announcement. The stock has now rallied around 9% in just two days following the Centre's decision to make electric vehicles the default choice for staff-car procurement by government ministries and departments.Ola Electric shares rose to Rs 37 apiece on NSE on Thursday morning. Notably, this is only the second time in a month the stock has crossed this level. The sharp 9% surge over the two days has added more than Rs 1,400 crore to the company’s market capitalisation, pushing it above Rs 17,150 crore.Also read | EV makers turn to family scooters to drive mass-market adoptionAll about the centre’s new EV procurement policyThe Finance Ministry has made electric vehicles (EVs) the "default and preferred choice" for the procurement of government staff cars in all ministries and departments of the Centre, with immediate effect. It also doubled the net dealer price ceiling for the procurement of EVs by central government ministries and departments to Rs 20 lakh, while that for ICE vehicles, including petrol, diesel and hybrid cars, has been fixed at Rs 10 lakh.The government also mandated preference to EVs in hiring cars for government use. The moves are aimed to promote electric mobility, reducing dependence on fossil fuels, and taking into account the prevailing market prices and lifecycle costs of vehicles."Going forward, Ministries and Departments shall ordinarily procure Electric Vehicles (EVs) at the time of condemnation or replacement of their existing ICE staff cars. EVs shall be the default and preferred choice for procurement," the official order reads.Also read | Centre's EV push puts electric mobility stocks in the fast laneOla Electric share priceAfter a flat market debut in August 2024, Ola shares rose to a lifetime high of Rs 157.40 apiece later that year. The stock subsequently lost momentum and fell to a lifetime low of Rs 22.25 in March 2026, nearly one-seventh of its peak value.The stock had fallen more than 62% from its 52-week high of Rs 59.20 apiece, hit in September last year, to a 52-week low of Rs 22.25 apiece in March this year. However, the stock subsequently staged a sharp recovery, doubling from that level in three months to hit a 52-week high of Rs 49.05 apiece in June this year. It has now pared some of the gains.Ola Electric shares gained over 4% in the past week and around 3% over the past month. articles.title: Debt Mutual Funds: What investors should know before investing
articles.summary: Debt mutual funds saw a net outflow of Rs 1.8 lakh crore in September, the highest monthly withdrawal in the first half of FY27. Despite this, they remain an important investment avenue for investors looking to park surplus money, manage short-term goals and diversify their portfolios. A look at how debt funds work and what investors should know before investing.WHAT ARE DEBT MUTUAL FUNDS?Debt mutual funds invest in fixed-income instruments such as government securities, treasury bills, corporate bonds, commercial paper and certificates of deposit. They aim to provide relatively stable returns while taking lower risk than equity funds. Debt funds generate returns in two ways. The first is through the interest earned on the bonds and other securities held in the portfolio. The second comes from changes in bond prices. When bond prices rise, fund managers can book gains by selling these securities.HOW SHOULD INVESTORS CHOOSE A DEBT FUND? The choice depends on the investment horizon, liquidity needs and ability to tolerate fluctuations in returns. Investors looking to park money for a few days or months may consider overnight or liquid funds. Those with a horizon of six months to two years may look at ultra-short duration, low duration or money-market funds. For investment horizons of three years or more, categories such as short-duration funds, corporate bond funds and banking & PSU debt funds may be suitable. Gilt funds and long-duration funds are generally more appropriate for investors who understand interest-rate cycles.Read more: Smallcap mutual fund inflows drop 29% MoM to Rs 6,407 crore in October. Should investors be cautious or continue investing?WHY DID DEBT FUNDS WITNESS LARGE OUTFLOWS IN SEPTEMBER? The large outflows were largely driven by liquidity requirements rather than a change in investor appetite for debt funds. These schemes are widely used by companies and institutional investors to park surplus cash for short periods. September is also a quarter-end month when companies usually withdraw money to meet working capital requirements, advance tax payments and other financial obligations.Read more: Debt mutual funds see sharp recovery in October as quarter-end outflows reverseARE DEBT FUNDS RISK-FREE? While debt funds are generally less volatile than equity funds, they are not risk-free. One key risk is interest-rate risk. When interest rates rise, bond prices fall, which can affect the value of a fund’s portfolio. The second is credit risk, which arises when a company or other issuer fails to repay its debt or interest on time. Funds investing in lower-rated corporate bonds generally carry higher credit risk.HOW DO INTEREST RATES AFFECT DEBT FUND RETURNS? Interest rates and bond prices move in opposite directions. When interest rates fall, existing bonds offering higher interest become more attractive to investors. As demand for these bonds rises, their prices generally move up. This, in turn, tends to benefit debt funds. When interest rates rise, bond prices usually decline, which can weigh on returns. Long-duration funds are usually more affected by interest-rate changes, while liquid and overnight funds tend to see smaller fluctuations.

articles.title: CoreWeave shares surge over 26%, spark rally in battered AI cloud stocks
articles.summary: CoreWeave shares surged more than 26% on Wednesday, fuelling a rally in battered AI cloud stocks after heavy infrastructure spending delivered strong revenue growth and the company signalled a retreat from the borrowing spree that had raised fears of an artificial intelligence bubble, Reuters reported.CoreWeave shares were trading at $61.61, up $12.88 or 26.43% over the previous close.The results also helped lift Nvidia, a major CoreWeave backer, by 2%. Nvidia had fallen sharply over the previous two sessions amid uncertainty surrounding CEO Jensen Huang following reports about his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to have ties to Beijing’s intelligence apparatus.Shares of other so-called neocloud companies, including Nebius and Iren, also rallied after weeks of pressure. Investors have worried that their debt-funded data-centre expansion could backfire if demand for AI computing weakens.For live updates on US Markets, click here“CoreWeave’s earnings directly addressed the fear that’s driven this whole selloff,” said Dan Sheehan, director of portfolio management at Telos Wealth Advisors, according to Reuters. “The neocloud that became the poster child for AI financing worries took real weight off the fear that had been the heart of the selloff.”Democrats’ sweep of last week’s US midterm elections had further unsettled the industry. Several victorious candidates campaigned for stricter regulation and moratoriums on new data-centre construction, including in Texas, a key market for the sector.CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told Reuters on Tuesday that increased regulatory scrutiny could slow data-centre development across the industry. However, he did not expect it to significantly affect the company’s expansion plans or raise costs.Intrator said CoreWeave’s planned capacity additions over the next year would remain unaffected.Also Read: Is AI wheel broken? Julius Baer flags 3 variables shaping AI investments ahead of Anthropic IPOThe company also said it would avoid unsecured debt markets following a recent surge in borrowing costs. Cash flow from existing contracts would cover repayments on both current and future debt, it added—a financing plan analysts described as credible.“CoreWeave delivered about the best quarter we could have asked for. Stats were good-to-great, funding concerns were addressed and the strategic moves make sense,” Bernstein analysts led by Madison Rezaei said in a client note.However, they warned that CoreWeave “will be among the first and hardest hit” once the shortage of AI computing capacity eases.The risks of mistiming AI investments were evident on Tuesday when SoftBank recorded a $3.7 billion write-down on non-refundable payments for equipment intended to power its US data centres. The charge contributed to a second-quarter net loss of $7 billion, the company’s first in nearly two years.Uncertainty surrounding Huang has also weighed on the AI sector. The controversy intensified on Tuesday after reports alleged that his relationship helped facilitate billions of dollars in Nvidia chip shipments to China.Republican US Senator Kevin Cramer, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, called on Huang to step down as Nvidia CEO.For now, CoreWeave’s results have given AI infrastructure investors some relief. Nebius, Iren, Oracle and Applied Digital climbed between 6% and 14%.With the exception of Nebius, the stocks had fallen between 32% and 48% this year through Tuesday. Nebius, by contrast, had gained 60%.Together, the companies—including CoreWeave—were on track to add about $36 billion in market value if the gains held. Nvidia alone was positioned to gain nearly $100 billion.Nebius is scheduled to report its results before Thursday’s opening bell.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. articles.summary: On November 16, the Reserve Bank of India will initiate a significant switch auction worth 250 billion rupees. This maneuver involves replacing six bonds that are set to mature between 2027 and 2029 with longer-term securities extending to maturity in 2062. articles.title: Bitcoin bull run ahead? 2023 pattern returns
articles.summary: Bitcoin (BTC USD) price prediction: Bitcoin's latest decline hasn't stopped one analyst from looking for signs of a recovery. Tim Warren believes the cryptocurrency is showing a pattern that appeared before previous bull runs. Even as investor sentiment weakens and money continues to leave US spot Bitcoin exchange traded funds (ETFs).Bitcoin (BTC USD) 200-day moving average brings back memories of previous market cyclesWarren reportedly pointed out to similarities between BTC USD current price movement & patterns from earlier market cycles. He pointed to the cryptocurrency breaking above its bear market trendline and 200-day moving average before returning to test that average, as per a Benzinga report.He said similar movements appeared during the 2014-2015 and 2018-2019 cycles. So Warren believes the current market is showing a comparable setup.Investor sentiment, meanwhile, has weakened. Bitcoin's Fear and Greed Index has entered extreme fear territory for the first time since August. However, the cryptocurrency was still trading 17% higher than the last time the index reached a similar level.Warren described the difference between sentiment and price performance as a healthy correction. He also said he was buying spot Bitcoin around its 200-day moving average.135736403BTC USD price outlook: Bitcoin analyst watches $72,900, $71,600 and $68,400Warren identified three price zones to watch if Bitcoin faces further selling pressure, $72,900, $71,600 and $68,400. He described these as "fair value gap zones".A decline towards $68,400 would not necessarily change his constructive outlook. However, a fall below the broader bear market low near $57,700 would reduce his confidence that the level would hold from 90% to around 70%.Warren has also moved away from relying on Bitcoin's traditional four-year halving cycle. He stopped following the model around 18 months ago after the current cycle's low arrived in July rather than October, which was the timing the model had suggested.He believes institutional capital now has a greater influence on Bitcoin's price movements than halving-related supply changes.Bitcoin ETF outflows fall for a third consecutive dayThe latest ETF figures show that investors are still pulling money from Bitcoin funds, although the pace of withdrawals has eased.US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $95 million in net outflows on November 10, according to Farside data cited by Cryptopolitan. Withdrawals had reached $430 million on November 5, $412 million on November 6 and $201 million on November 9.Tuesday's figure was approximately 53% lower than the previous session. November's cumulative withdrawals, however, had reached around $1.6 billion.BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded $78.2 million in outflows, while Fidelity's FBTC lost $36.8 million. Morgan Stanley's Bitcoin Trust ETF (MSBT) attracted $20 million.IBIT also extended its outflow streak to eight consecutive sessions, with approximately $1.73 billion leaving the fund since October 30.135714823Stock ETFs attract billions as Bitcoin funds face withdrawalsThe movement in Bitcoin ETFs contrasts with the strong inflows into US-listed stock funds.Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas said US-listed ETFs attracted approximately $12 billion per day over five trading sessions. All 17 funds with the highest inflows during that period invested in stocks.Vanguard's S&P 500 ETF (VOO), Invesco's Nasdaq-100 ETF (QQQ) and BlackRock's iShares Core S&P 500 ETF (IVV) were among the largest beneficiaries.The inflows came during an AI-led stock market selloff that wiped out Bitcoin's post-midterm rally.Bitcoin was trading at $73,000 level, as of Wednesday.135714063
